revision.revised_text:
PRODUCTION SERVICES AGREEMENT

Date/Effective Date: March 4, 2026

This Production Services Agreement (“Agreement”) is between Harbor Media Inc. (“Client”) and Luna Park Studio (“Vendor”).

1. Scope of Services

Vendor will perform production services described in Statement of Work (SOW), Exhibit A, and technical specifications in Appendix 1, all incorporated by reference. If Exhibit A, Appendix 1, or any other referenced attachment is unavailable, incomplete, or inconsistent at signing, the parties will work in good faith to complete and approve it in writing within 30 days after the Effective Date. Vendor has no obligation to perform services that are not described in a signed SOW, Appendix 1, or other written approval signed by both parties, and Client requests outside those written documents are not binding unless Vendor agrees in writing to the scope, price, and schedule impact.

2. Fees and Payment

Total project fee is $18,000. Client pays 30% deposit and remainder within Net 30 days after invoice receipt. Late payments accrue interest at 1.5% per month or the maximum rate permitted by law, whichever is less, from the due date until paid.

3. Term and Termination

Term starts on the Effective Date and continues until completion. Client may terminate for convenience on 7 days notice. Upon termination for convenience, Client will pay Vendor for all services performed, deliverables completed or in progress, approved expenses, and non-cancelable commitments incurred before the effective termination date, less amounts previously paid. Vendor may suspend work for undisputed amounts that remain unpaid more than 10 days after written notice and a 5-business-day opportunity to cure, and Vendor may terminate for nonpayment if undisputed amounts remain unpaid 30 days after written overdue notice.

4. Intellectual Property

Upon full payment, final approved deliverables are assigned to Client. Vendor retains ownership of pre-existing tools and portfolio rights unless prohibited by Client in writing.

5. Confidentiality

Each party will keep the other party’s Confidential Information private during the term of this Agreement and for two years after the Agreement ends. “Confidential Information” means non-public business, technical, financial, creative, customer, vendor, pricing, production, marketing, or strategic information disclosed by or on behalf of a party that is marked confidential or reasonably should be understood to be confidential under the circumstances. Confidential Information does not include information that is publicly available without breach of this Agreement, already known by the receiving party without a duty of confidentiality, independently developed without use of the disclosing party’s Confidential Information, or rightfully received from a third party without a duty of confidentiality. A receiving party may disclose Confidential Information if required by law, court order, or governmental authority, provided it gives prompt notice to the disclosing party when legally permitted and limits the disclosure to what is required.

6. Indemnity and Liability

Each party will indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other party from third-party claims, damages, liabilities, costs, and reasonable attorneys’ fees arising from the indemnifying party’s breach of this Agreement, negligence, or willful misconduct. Client will also indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Vendor from third-party claims arising from Client-provided materials, instructions, approvals, or content, provided Vendor used them as authorized by Client. Except for fraud, willful misconduct, confidentiality breach, indemnification obligations, and Client’s payment obligations, each party’s liability is capped at amounts paid or payable under this Agreement.

7. Disputes and Governing Law

Any dispute first goes to mediation in Seattle, Washington. If the dispute is not resolved within 30 days after a written request for mediation, either party may bring the dispute in the state or federal courts located in Seattle, Washington, and each party consents to jurisdiction and venue in those courts. Arbitration is not required unless both parties agree in writing after the dispute arises. Nothing in this Agreement waives either party’s right to a jury trial unless the parties separately agree in writing after the dispute arises. Governing law is the State of Washington.

8. Assignment and Subcontracting

Vendor may subcontract portions of work to qualified contractors but remains responsible for deliverables. Neither party may assign this Agreement without written consent, except in a merger.

9. Warranties

Vendor warrants deliverables will substantially conform to written specifications for 30 days after delivery.

10. Restrictions

Nothing in this Agreement creates any non-compete, non-solicitation, exclusivity, right of first refusal, or similar restriction on either party. Vendor remains free to provide services to other clients, including clients in the same or similar industries, provided Vendor does not use or disclose Client’s Confidential Information in violation of this Agreement.

Signed:

Harbor Media Inc. ___________________

Luna Park Studio ___________________
